👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Kill switch does not reach installs with "Send diagnostics" off (or offline) (confidence high)**

The runbook says that with the flag enabled at 0% "every build reads `false` and the next take uses Chromium capture". That isn't true for every install. `isFlagEnabled` returns the fallback, now `true`, whenever PostHog isn't started (`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/analytics/analytics-client.ts:77`). PostHog starts only when `diagnosticsEnabled` is on (`analytics-client.ts:28-31`), and users can turn that setting off (`settings.service.ts:159-162`). A build without `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` also never starts PostHog, and neither does a launch with no cached flags and no network.

Before this PR the fallback was `false`, so this gap didn't matter. Now those users keep native capture no matter what PostHog says, and the doc reads as if the switch is universal. Say in the runbook that the kill switch only reaches installs with diagnostics on that have loaded flags. If that coverage isn't acceptable for an incident, the remaining escape hatch is a release.

**Refresh the kill-switch value before selecting the transport.** PostHog refreshes flags every five minutes by default. A take before the next refresh can still use native capture after operators set the flag to 0%, contrary to the runbook. Refresh and await the flag before selecting the transport. Preserve the existing override and offline fallback behavior.

**Keep the kill switch available when diagnostics are off.** In packaged builds, disabling Send diagnostics makes `isFlagEnabled` return the new `true` default. Eligible recordings can then use native capture even when the PostHog flag is at 0%. Provide a disable path that does not depend on diagnostics and preserves the user's privacy choice.
